New Product Introduction (NPI) Execution

Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) Relationship Management

- Support NPI onboarding activities at CMO sites, including capacity assessments, technology transfers, validation batch scheduling, and commercial scale-up readiness reviews.
- Align with global supply planning on production schedules, minimum order quantities (MOQs), lead times, and change order processes with CMO partners.
- Proactively identify and mitigate supply risks arising from CMO capacity constraints, raw material shortages, packaging issues or regulatory changes.

Demand Forecasting & Supply Planning
- Jointly with commercial develop robust demand forecasts for new product introductions in collaboration with brand managers, sales operations, and finance, incorporating market intelligence, historical analogs, and launch channel strategies.

- Manage the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) input process for all NPI SKUs, maintaining accuracy and version control of demand signals shared with CMOs and internal stakeholders.
- Execute supply rebalancing and phase-in/phase-out strategies to minimize excess and obsolete inventory risk during product transitions.

Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)
- Partner with brand and regulatory teams to assess the supply chain impact of formula updates, label changes, and regulatory submissions, ensuring continuity of supply throughout.
- Maintain accurate and current SKU master data, bill of materials (BOM), and supplier records within ERP and PLM systems.
- Contribute to portfolio rationalization initiatives, providing supply chain data and analysis to support brand and business decisions.

- Champion continuous improvement initiatives targeting NPI lead time reduction, CMO performance improvement, and planning process efficiency.

- Collaborate with the quality team to resolve non-conformances, deviations, and CAPA actions involving CMO partners and NPI activities.

Strategic Thinking
- Ability to anticipate downstream supply chain implications of business decisions and develop proactive mitigation strategies.

Cross-Functional Leadership
- Skilled at aligning diverse stakeholders across brand, R&D, regulatory, operations, and finance without direct authority.

Results Orientation
- Demonstrates a consistent track record of delivering complex launches on time and within scope and budget.

Analytical Rigor
- Applies structured, data-driven approaches to forecasting, planning, and performance management.

CMO Partnership Management
- Builds trust-based, performance-driven relationships with external manufacturing partners.

Adaptability & Resilience
- Thrives in a dynamic, high-growth environment where priorities and timelines evolve rapidly.

Communication Excellence
- Conveys complex supply chain concepts clearly and concisely to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Continuous Improvement Mindset
- Actively identifies inefficiencies and drives process improvements across NPI and lifecycle management workflows.

- Marketing Brand Management, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Finance, Quality, Packaging, Manufacturing

Â

- Minimum 5â7 years of supply chain experience, with at least 3 years in a New Product Introduction, product launch, or contract manufacturing management capacity.
- Demonstrated experience managing CMO or third-party manufacturing relationships, including capacity planning, technology transfer, and performance management.
- Proven track record of executing end-to-end NPI projects within the consumer products, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, medical aesthetics, or personal care industries.
- Strong proficiency in demand planning and supply planning processes, including participation in S&OP cycles.

Job Description

PRIMARY FUNCTION/OBJECTIVE
To provide district sales team with leadership, direction and resources to ensure revenue target is achieved; and to liaise with Marketing, Key Account Managers, and Customer Excellence to ensure that short and long term sales responsibilities, strategies, and programs are carried out.
CORE JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Specific Duties
- Implement Business Unit (BU) strategies to accelerate products penetration to eligible patients, and to maximize customer impact via multi-channels to ensure sales goals and targets are achieved. Develop sales plans for district; contribute to the development of annual Plan and Latest Best Estimates for BU, and convey objectives and milestones clearly to team so that he/she can lead others in the execution of activities to achieve desired sales results. Communicate closely with Marketing, Key Account Managers, Customer Excellence and sales colleagues to share information and help execute plans and programs across functions.
- Monitor market trends, including customersâ insight and competitor intelligence in assigned territory. Proactively analyze and evaluate data, input, and proposals from a variety of sources to confirm alignment and/or determine adjustments to plans and/or tactics. Stay current on a wide-range of business and industry concerns and use this knowledge to identify key drivers. Furnish General Manager and Marketing with information on industry trends, customer attitudes, competitive activities, market opportunities and threats. Assess and prioritize potential business growth opportunities.
- Utilize selling skills and develop account strategies and tactical approaches to ensure customer needs are met by the BUâs products where possible. Influence the development and enhancement of relationships with customers especially Key Opinion Leaders.
- Implement and oversee inventory management processes in District in strict accordance with Company procedures governing product controls including expiry.
- Address product experiences in timely fashion in accordance with Company policy.
- Hire and develop sales staff in his/her district. Serve as a positive role model by exhibiting ethical principles and behaviors, and insist others follow this lead. Provide employees with experiences and assignments that allow them to grow their capabilities. Coach and evaluate team members on performance, enhancement of their strength and improvement of developmental needs. Anticipate position openings by building the talent base and having candidates ready for appropriate opportunities. Support affiliate EHS policies related to driving safety and biohazard safety, etc.
- Represent AbbVie in a professional manner that aligns with Company image, ensuring activities comply with Legal and AbbVieâs Code of Business Conduct. Support compliance and ethical practice initiatives by consistently being a leader in this area. Review compliance metrics and drives behavior to constantly reinforce initiatives and desired outcomes
- Successfully complete new-hire training program; maintain professional knowledge via self-study and participation in internal and external education events.

Professional Competencies

âª Individual Leadership/Influencing
- Use appropriate interpersonal styles and methods to inspire and guide individuals (direct reports, peers, and superiors) toward goal achievement; modify behavior to accommodate tasks, situations, and individuals involved.
- Achieve organizational goals through co-operative action with others.
- Use relationship skills to encourage involvement and provide support while maintaining accountability.
- Present suggestions and point of view in an appropriate and convincing manner.

âª Teamwork/Collaboration

senior managers) to accomplish organizational goals; take actions that respect the needs and

contributions of others; contribute to and accepting the consensus; subordinating own objectives to the objectives of the organization or team.
- Work co-operatively with other District Managers/Product Managers/BU Manager to accomplish organizational goals
- Communicate changes or problems to peers, team members or others at sales/marketing meetings.
- Establish team spirit through collaboration and team activities.

âª Planning and Organizing/Work Management

Establish a course of action for self and others to accomplish a specific goal; plan proper assignments of personnel and appropriate allocation of resources.
- Schedule and co-ordinate sales meetings, review periods and training schedules for representatives and product managers.
- Allocate time and resources to colleagues from finance, marketing, and training.
- Allocate expense and sales budgets at the district level and for representatives
- Establish short- and long-term goals for the district and for representatives within that district, based on BU strategic focus.

âª Analysis and Problem Assessment

Secure relevant information and identify key issues and relationships from a base of information; relate and compare data from different sources; identify cause-effect relationships.
- Review expenses, sales reports, account data and trends to identify problems and act accordingly.
- Understand and resolve personal or organizational problems amongst team members or peers.

âª Developing Organizational Talent

Develop subordinatesâ skills and competencies by planning effective development activities related to current and future jobs.
- Design formal plans for individualsâ short term and long-term career development at time of appraisal.
- Encourage individuals to develop skills they might need for career growth by setting standards or delegating.
- Provide constructive feedback on development progress through field reports.
- Design appropriate developmental projects for direct reports to be presented at sales meetings.

âª Coaching

Facilitate the development of othersâ knowledge and skills; providing timely feedback and guidance to help them reach goals.
- Express confidence and feedback in representativesâ ability to perform a delegated activity or see through a strategic initiative.
- Establish clear benchmarks and standards for representatives to gauge individual performance by setting yearly goals and quarterly focus at appraisals.
- Help people look for new ways to solve old problems through field visits and brainstorming sessions at meetings.

âª Organizational Awareness

Having and using knowledge of systems, situations, procedures, and culture inside the organization to identify potential organizational problems and opportunities; perceiving the impact and the implications of decisions on other components of the organization.
- Understand the organizationâs structure, operations, decision-making channels, planning processes and financial budget control systems.
- Understand the organization and separate BUâs direction and system of operation.

âª Delegation of Authority and Responsibility

Allocate decision-making authority and task responsibilities to appropriate subordinates; utilizing

subordinatesâ time, skills and potential effectively.

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY
The Brand Manager â Eyecare will shape and accelerate the growth of AbbVieâs Eyecare portfolio in Thailand, with end-to-end accountability for brand strategy, launch excellence, lifecycle management, and in-market performance. Combining strategic thinking with hands-on execution, this role converts customer, patient, market, and competitive insights into differentiated plans that strengthen brand value and deliver sustainable business growth.
As the strategic lead for the assigned portfolio, the Brand Manager will influence across a matrix organization and align Sales, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Finance, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Business Excellence, and Area/Global teams behind a clear brand ambition. The role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact launches, build trusted external partnerships, develop new growth opportunities, and improve outcomes for patientsâwhile maintaining the highest standards of ethics, quality, and compliance.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Marketing, Product and Launch Management
- Set the long-term brand ambition and own the end-to-end strategy for assigned Eyecare products across launch, growth, maturity, and lifecycle optimization.
- Translate global and Area strategy into a locally relevant, insight-led annual brand plan with clear priorities, investment choices, milestones, and measures of success.
- Lead launch excellence for new products, indications, and line extensions, from early market shaping and readiness planning through execution and post-launch optimization.
- Develop a deep understanding of patients, customers, the treatment pathway, market access dynamics, competitors, and emerging trends; commission market research where needed and convert insights into action.
- Define differentiated positioning, value propositions, segmentation, targeting, channel strategy, and core messages for priority customer groups.
- Design and execute integrated, customer-centric and omnichannel campaigns that strengthen engagement, support field execution, and maximize brand impact.
- Identify portfolio, indication, market-development, pricing, packaging, and partnership opportunities that can unlock sustainable growth and long-term value.
- Establish performance dashboards and lead regular business reviews; use leading and lagging indicators to identify risks, optimize investment, and initiate timely corrective action.
- Provide senior stakeholders with clear, decision-oriented updates on performance, strategic choices, opportunities, risks, and progress against milestones.

Budget, Forecast and Supply Management
- Build and manage the annual brand budget, allocating resources to the highest-value opportunities and maintaining disciplined control of spend.
- Partner with Finance and Sales to develop robust sales forecasts, scenario plans, and business cases grounded in market assumptions and performance drivers.
- Recommend pricing and pricing-adjustment strategies that balance patient access, competitiveness, revenue growth, and gross-profit objectives.
- Track investment effectiveness and forecast accuracy, proactively addressing variances and reallocating resources when priorities change.
- Collaborate with Supply Chain and Logistics on demand planning, inventory management, sample availability, and continuity of supply, particularly during launch and growth phases.

Scientific Engagement and External Partnership
- Partner with Medical Affairs and Area/Global teams to ensure brand strategy is informed by robust science, relevant evidence, and evolving standards of care.
- Build and sustain trusted, compliant relationships with key opinion leaders, professional societies, healthcare institutions, and relevant patient or health organizations.
- Develop local external-engagement and expert-development plans that support education, scientific exchange, market shaping, and responsible brand growth.
- Contribute to advisory boards, speaker programs, congresses, and scientific meetings in close partnership with Medical Affairs and in full compliance with applicable requirements.

Training and Capability Development
- Translate strategy into high-quality product, disease-state, customer-engagement, and launch-readiness training for AbbVie and distributor field teams.
- Partner with Sales Force Effectiveness, Training, Medical Affairs, and Sales leadership to identify capability gaps and deliver practical learning that improves execution.
- Ensure all training content is scientifically accurate, customer-relevant, engaging, and aligned with approved brand strategy and compliance standards.
- Select and lead external agencies with clear briefs, governance, timelines, quality standards, budgets, and performance indicators.

Cross-Functional Leadership and Collaboration
- Lead the cross-functional brand team and create shared ownership of priorities, decisions, milestones, and outcomes across Sales, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Finance, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Business Excellence, and other partners.
- Influence without direct authority, constructively challenge assumptions, resolve trade-offs, and maintain momentum in a complex matrix environment.
- Partner with Regulatory Affairs to prioritize new-product, indication, and packaging submissions and support readiness for approval and launch.
- Collaborate with Market Access on value creation and appropriate engagement with priority accounts, institutions, and payers.
- Translate brand strategy into focused, actionable guidance for the field and partner with Sales leadership on goal setting, prioritization, capability needs, and performance tracking.
- Maintain a strong external orientation through regular field visits and customer engagement, using first-hand insights to improve strategy and execution.

Quality, Compliance and Governance
- Ensure all marketing, launch, digital, agency, and promotional activities comply with AbbVie policies, approval processes, industry codes, and applicable laws and regulations in Thailand.

Job Description

Purpose
The Site Supply Chain Manager is a hands-on operational leader responsible for the day-to-day execution of supply chain activities supporting site operations. Reporting to the Associate Director, Materials Management, this role leads site planning, scheduling, inventory management, master data, and logistics activities to ensure materials, capacity, and resources are available to support production and business requirements.
The Site Supply Chain Manager works closely with manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, quality, engineering, supply planning, and warehouse teams to identify challenges, resolve issues, and drive actions to completion. This role requires a strong presence within site operations, regular engagement with cross-functional teams, and a willingness to work through operational details to support reliable execution.
As the primary supply chain representative for the site, the manager communicates priorities, risks, and recovery plans, aligns stakeholders on actions and decisions, and helps establish the processes, routines, and team capabilities needed to support a growing medical device manufacturing operation. The role balances daily operational execution with team development, process improvement, and continuous problem solving.
Responsibilities
1. Lead and develop the site supply chain team.
Directly manage site supply chain personnel responsible for planning, scheduling, inventory management, master data, and logistics activities. Establish performance expectations, monitor workloads, provide coaching and development, conduct performance reviews, and create a positive and accountable work environment. Participate in hiring, onboarding, and talent development activities as needed.
2. Own daily site supply chain execution.
Lead daily and weekly reviews of material availability, inventory position, capacity readiness, schedule performance, and logistics requirements. Establish priorities, assign actions, and track progress to completion. Maintain a visible presence in site operations and work directly with team members and site partners to identify and resolve constraints affecting execution.
3. Oversee production scheduling and schedule adherence.
Provide direction and oversight for developing and maintaining an executable production schedule that supports customer commitments and operational objectives. Partner with manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, quality, and planning resources to assess readiness, manage constraints, and support schedule execution. Ensure proposed changes within the locked schedule period are evaluated for impact and managed through established approval and communication processes.
4. Oversee materials, inventory, and capacity readiness.
Lead efforts to identify material shortages, inventory risks, and capacity constraints that could impact production. Review inventory levels, planning requirements, and material availability to support site operating needs while minimizing disruptions. Facilitate regular reviews of manufacturing capacity, labor availability, equipment constraints, and material readiness to identify risks and coordinate mitigation plans. Partner closely with purchasing/procurement to align material requirements, supplier commitments, and changing site priorities.
5. Lead operational problem solving and recovery actions.
Serve as the primary escalation point for supply chain issues affecting site execution, including shortages, scheduling conflicts, inventory risks, capacity constraints, and logistics disruptions. Bring together the appropriate stakeholders to assess impacts, establish action ownership, and coordinate recovery plans. Drive root cause investigations and ensure corrective actions are implemented and sustained.
6. Represent supply chain in site operations discussions.
Communicate supply chain performance, material readiness, inventory position, capacity risks, and recovery plans to the Associate Director, Materials Management and site leadership teams. Align stakeholders on priorities, timing, responsibilities, and operational decisions. Ensure changes in business or operational requirements are reflected in supply chain activities.
7. Oversee logistics and partner with warehouse leadership.
Provide oversight of logistics activities that support inbound material flow, internal material movement, and outbound shipments. Partner closely with warehouse leadership to coordinate priorities, resolve operational issues, and improve material flow throughout the facility. Ensure effective coordination between supply chain and warehouse functions to support production requirements.
8. Establish effective planning and master data processes.
Support the development and execution of planning routines, standard work, escalation processes, and operating procedures that enable consistent execution. Ensure master data is accurate, maintained according to established controls, and supports effective ERP/MRP execution. Partner with site teams to improve planning processes, system utilization, and operational discipline.
9. Support compliant material operations.
Ensure all supply chain activities are executed in compliance with site procedures and quality requirements for regulated medical device manufacturing. Partner with quality, manufacturing, purchasing/procurement, and warehouse teams to ensure material status, traceability, shelf-life requirements, and approved changes are properly managed. Support audit readiness and resolution of supply chain-related quality issues.
10. Manage performance and continuous improvement.
Monitor and improve key performance indicators including material availability, inventory health, schedule adherence, capacity readiness, logistics performance, and master data accuracy. Use performance trends, operational feedback, and root cause analysis to improve reliability, reduce recurring issues, and support continuous improvement initiatives across the site.

- Bachelor's degree in Production Operations Management, Logistics Management, Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, or Supply chain management disciplines preferred, or equivalent work experience
- Strong teamwork skills required to work effectively in a team environment and establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external supply chain partners.
